all_of: a server-side image pipeline interpolates a user value into a PIL.ImageMath.eval expression
Pillow is 8.4.0 or older, so eval/exec remain callable inside ImageMath expressions
the response can carry back some artifact the pipeline produces
any_of: an upload endpoint that accepts arbitrary PIL-openable formats and rejects others as bad image file
a color or alpha parameter that lands inside a formatted expression string

chain.action: accept any PIL-openable image (PNG/GIF confirmed, EPS rejected) and pass one 1x1 RGBA baseline to learn the response contract
chain.why: the pipeline runs make_alpha only after Image.open succeeds, so the baseline defines the cheapest valid request

chain.action: confirm the ImageMath.eval sandbox escape with a time differential: background[0] = eval("__import__('time').sleep(6)") delays the response to ~7.5s instead of ~1s
chain.why: Pillow <= 8.4.0 lets eval be called inside an ImageMath expression (CVE-2022-22817); the raw-arithmetic string fails validation, only the eval(...) wrapper survives, so the timing probe is the discriminating one

chain.action: copy the flag into the app's own static folder: background[0] = eval("__import__('shutil').copy('/flag.txt', __import__('flask').current_app.static_folder + '/f.txt')")
chain.why: flask.current_app is available inside the request context, so the app reveals its own static folder instead of guessing paths, and the static route then serves the flag as an HTTP GET

chain.action: GET /static/f.txt and read the flag from the live response, then remove the copied artifact with os.remove(static_folder + '/f.txt')
chain.why: the response channel is already reachable, and write-shaped probes on a shared instance must be cleaned up

first_confirming_probe.request: background[0] = eval("__import__('time').sleep(6)") compared with a ~1s baseline request
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the response stays at the baseline duration (eval not executed), or every string in background is rejected before the pipeline

blast_radius: arbitrary python runs inside the challenge container; a cp or rm with a wrong path can disturb app state, and an eval(exit()) kills the single-process dev server permanently

verification.evidence: flag string read from /static/f.txt on the rebuilt deployment Supporting observation: response time near 7s instead of ~1s

reuse_when: a server-side pipeline formats user values into an ImageMath or similar sandboxed expression
Pillow or another sandbox exposes eval/exec as builtins in the compiled namespace
the app can write into a folder the same instance serves back over HTTP
known_traps: raw arithmetic strings in the injection slot are rejected before execution; the working payload needs the eval("...") wrapper
a fast 400 can hide a command that already executed as a side effect; verify the write result downstream
quoted shells inside the f-string need exactly one escaping level per layer or the whole expression never parses
the static_folder is guessable but not required: flask.current_app hands out the real path from inside the request
class budget accounting counts the exploratory probes; keep falsifiers separate so the confirmed mechanism keeps a probe slot for the exfil round
